### Review Summary

The branch successfully implements the `OpenAIAsyncProvider` to support non-blocking streaming token generation via `openai.AsyncOpenAI`. The code structurally matches the interfaces and mirrors the logic of the legacy synchronous provider, ensuring safe coexistence and a clean migration path. The primary concerns are an unskipped integration test that will fail full-suite test runs on unprovisioned machines, and the preservation of a legacy limitation where streamed responses bypass the minimum word count check.

**Files Reviewed:** 7
**Findings:** 0 Critical, 2 Warning, 4 Suggestion

### Findings

#### Warning Findings

[W-01] Streamed text bypasses minimum word count enforcement
Category: Correctness
Severity: Warning
File: src/infrastructure/providers/openai_async_provider.py
Lines: 147-156
Description: In `generate_text`, when `stream=True`, the code streams chunks and returns the accumulated string immediately. This bypasses the `min_word_count` check and continuation prompt applied to non-streaming requests. While this mirrors the exact limitation in the legacy `OpenAICompatibleProvider`, it means streamed responses can silently fall short of requested length thresholds without recovery.
Suggestion: Document this limitation in the feature notes. To fix it technically, streaming paths could accumulate tokens and silently execute a non-streaming continuation prompt if the threshold isn't met, streaming those new tokens as well.

[W-02] Live integration test lacks environment skip protection
Category: Testing
Severity: Warning
File: tests/integration/test_openai_async_provider_live.py
Lines: 33
Description: The live test does not use the `llm_available` skip fixture (as explicitly noted in the documentation updates). While running `pytest` limits scope to `tests/unit/`, running `pytest tests/` or `pytest tests/integration/` will unconditionally execute this test. It will fail outright (rather than cleanly skipping) if an LLM server isn't running locally, breaking full-suite CI/dev runs.
Suggestion: Apply the `pytest.mark.skipif` or the session-scoped `llm_available` fixture to this test class so it skips gracefully during runs on unprovisioned environments.

#### Suggestions

[S-01] Redundant exception handling blocks
Category: Style
Severity: Suggestion
File: src/infrastructure/providers/openai_async_provider.py
Lines: 174-178
Description: The `generate_text` method catches specific OpenAI exceptions (`APIConnectionError`, `APITimeoutError`, `APIStatusError`) and raises a `ModelProviderError` with a formatted error message. The immediately following generic `Exception` catch block does exactly the same thing, raising an identically formatted error message. The same redundancy appears in `stream_text` (lines 235-238).
Suggestion: Consolidate into a single `except Exception as exc:` block, or provide a distinct error message for the specific OpenAI exceptions.

[S-02] Dead regex substitution code
Category: Correctness
Severity: Suggestion
File: src/infrastructure/providers/openai_async_provider.py
Lines: 93
Description: The fourth substitution rule in `_filter_think_tags` (`re.sub(r"(.*?)</think>.*", r"\1", ...)`) is unreachable dead code. The immediately preceding rule (`re.sub(r"</think>.*", "", ...)`) already removes everything from an unopened `</think>` tag to the end of the string, leaving no closing tags for the final regex to match.
Suggestion: Remove the fourth regex rule since it provides no additional filtering.

[S-03] Documentation list of supported providers is missing the new async key
Category: Documentation
Severity: Suggestion
File: docs/README.md
Lines: 15
Description: The "Runtime Stack" section lists "Supported provider keys are `openai_compatible`, `ollama`, `lm_studio`, and `llama_cpp`;". The PR explicitly implements a new provider that identifies as `openai_async` via `get_supported_providers()`, but this key was not added to the README list.
Suggestion: Add `openai_async` to the supported keys list.

[S-04] Test specifies incorrect provider key in ModelConfig
Category: Testing
Severity: Suggestion
File: tests/integration/test_openai_async_provider_live.py
Lines: 43
Description: The integration test instantiates `ModelConfig` with `provider="openai_compatible"`. Although the `OpenAIAsyncProvider` class doesn't internally validate the `provider` field of the config it receives, the config object should logically specify `openai_async` to match the target under test.
Suggestion: Change `provider="openai_compatible"` to `provider="openai_async"`.

### Overall Assessment

The PR cleanly implements the necessary `AsyncOpenAI` infrastructure without modifying existing synchronous constraints. The code is readable, heavily typed, and handles parameter manipulation correctly. It is ready for merge once the integration test is protected by a skip fixture to prevent breaking environment-independent test runs, and the minor warnings/suggestions are addressed or deferred.
